gaps.gap: One government, two ids. In a township-governed town, the law chain keys the township by its government-unit id, but the budget keys the same government `place:<geoid>`. U2's single bodyJurisdiction has to settle this. Today the township board's budget-line acts already land nowhere.
gaps.evidence: budgets.ts:671: city = local.municipal[0] ?? local.townships[0], with id `place:${geoid}` (:722). laws-starting.ts:110-115 and legislature.ts:5000-5009 put the township board's law at unit.id. In enact (legislature.ts:5110-5124), amendBudget(governmentId: jurisdiction) finds no government (budgets.ts:1796-1798 returns null). payProjectGrant also returns early (:2146-2149). budgetChambers matches the board only by level (legislature.ts:1222-1229, `gov.level === 'city' && office.level === 'township'`). A read-only probe over src/core2/data/places/localities.json found 4,382 of 32,350 localities township-governed: municipal empty, township board built. Puerto Rico has the same split: its budget government is `county:72xxx` (budgets.ts:689-716, comment 'the law chain holds no county for it').
gaps.fix: bodyJurisdiction returns the law key. Add a second function, budgetGovernmentOf(api, officeId), or a field on the government row, that maps a body to its budget id. enact's amendBudget and payProjectGrant use it, and so does budgetChambers. Register a stopgap if the township-board budget-line fix is deferred. Test with a drawn township-governed place (CT, NJ, PA, MI) and a Puerto Rico place.

gaps.fix: Export bodyJurisdiction(api, officeId) from legislature.ts. billJurisdiction calls it with bill.bodyOfficeId. localMeeting's `own`, recordHomeRule's target, the emit helper, budgetChambers and votesAreTownNews all call it too. Drop the `?? chain.townPlaceId` fallback, which writes an entity id as a session jurisdiction.

gaps.gap: Speed: the settledness, current-amount and stance reads U2 changes run once per member, often several times per member per vote. The maps price them as 'one Set.has per row'.

Have lastEnactment query bySeries [jurisdiction, series] for each member of the set, not filter bySeriesOnly. Measure with npm run speed:year against the 20% bar on the same base.

wrong.claim: Legislature map, countyOfBody: today it 'misfiles in a town whose largest-land county has no county government (Connecticut parts, Virginia independent-city parts)'. Its risks section says the fix moves the board's ordinances from countyGeoids[0] to its own county, and that 'both are chain levels'.
wrong.evidence: A read-only probe over all 32,350 localities found 328 towns whose county board's county is not countyGeoids[0]. In 323 of them the chain has no county level at all, and 292 of those are in Puerto Rico. Example: 7200186 Aceitunas has levels US, US-PR, place:7200186, countyGeoids [], and a county-board office at municipio:72099. Today countyOfBody returns null there (legislature.ts:5011-5024), so billReach gives 'city' and billJurisdiction gives `place:<geoid>`, a chain level. With the proposed `county:${governmentUnit(...).countyGeoid}`, the PR municipio's own legislature lands at county:72099. That is not a chain level, so under U2's gates its ordinances never take effect (lawTookEffect), leave the town's wire, and lose office.voted and interest groups. Connecticut builds no county board at all.
wrong.correction: A body with coversTown must resolve to a chain level. Either keep today's mapping for coversTown boards, or add the governing municipio or county to lawChainForPlace's county levels when countyGeoidsForPlace is empty (this changes Puerto Rico's chain; name it and re-baseline tests that draw Puerto Rico). Fix the risks line: the affected set is Puerto Rico plus about 31 towns missing from the 2020 place-county parts, not Connecticut and Virginia.
